mainTopic: ביעור of שביעית produce: the three lands, fruit taken out of ארץ ישראל, and whether unripe fruit may be destroyed
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: you may keep eating dates as long as some are still within reach of animals, but dates hidden among thorns do not count. The גמרא then quotes a משנה that splits ארץ ישראל into three lands for ביעור (יהודה, עבר הירדן, גליל). You may keep eating a crop in a land until it is gone from the last region of that land. The source is the פסוק 'ולבהמתך ולחיה אשר בארצך': you may keep produce at home only while wild animals can still find it in the field. Wild animals do not cross from one land to another, so each land is judged on its own. A ברייתא then argues about שביעית fruit taken out of ארץ ישראל. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it must be brought back for ביעור, and the גמרא shows how the same פסוק can teach both rules. In a story, רב ספרא gets two opposite reports of רבי אבהו's ruling and relies on the more precise one, from רב הונא; רב יוסף mocks him for picking the lenient view. Finally, the גמרא asks how רבי אילעאי could cut down a palm with unripe שביעית dates. That question leads to a debate over whether very young fruit already counts as fruit, and רב שימי's proof from a משנה about cutting trees continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Dates still reachable by animals versus dates hidden among thorns
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the ברייתא about dates. You may keep eating based on dates stuck between palm branches, but not based on dates stuck among thorns.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may continue eating dates because of the dates caught between the palm branches. But one may not continue eating because of the dates caught among the thorn bushes.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a ברייתא that started on the previous daf. It tells us which leftover dates still count as 'available', so that the obligation of ביעור has not yet begun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates caught between palm branches can still be reached by animals, so the crop has not truly ended in the field and you may keep eating. Dates stuck among thorns cannot be reached by animals, so they do not count, and ביעור applies. The test is whether the fruit is still available to animals in the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm branches. Fallen dates often get stuck between them, where animals can still reach them.
Thorn branches or thorny shrubs. Animals cannot reach dates that fall in there.
Removal. Once a crop of שביעית is gone from the field, you must stop keeping that produce at home.

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the end of a ברייתא from the previous daf. It is not the start of a new discussion. The new topic begins in the next step with 'תנן התם'.

phrases.english: One may eat based on those [dates] between the palm branches,
phrases.notes: These dates are still reachable by animals, so the crop has not ended.

phrases.english: but one may not eat based on those between the thorn branches.
phrases.notes: Animals cannot get to these, so they do not count as available.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the ברייתא from the end of the previous daf about when dates require ביעור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit counts as still available, so eating may continue, only if animals can actually reach it.

steps.title: The משנה of the three lands for ביעור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת שביעית. ארץ ישראל is divided into three lands for ביעור, and each land has three smaller regions. You may keep eating in each land until the crop is gone from its last region.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: There are three lands for ביעור: יהודה, עבר הירדן, and the גליל. Each of these has three smaller regions inside it. Why did the חכמים say three lands for ביעור? So that people may keep eating in each land until the crop runs out in the last region of that land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה from מסכת שביעית. It sets out the map of how ביעור is measured: by three large lands, not by the whole country and not by each small region.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside each big land there are three smaller regions (mountains, valley, plain). These smaller regions do not each count on their own. As long as the crop exists in any one of them, you may eat it anywhere in that land. But the three big lands are separate: a crop still growing in the גליל does not help someone in יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We learned there.' This introduces a משנה from a different מסכת.
Three lands: the three separate zones of ארץ ישראל for ביעור.
The land east of the Jordan River.
Until the last one runs out: when the crop is gone from the final region of that land.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. The three small regions inside each land do NOT count separately; one of them can keep eating permitted for all. The three big lands DO count separately.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical scope of ביעור. To know when a crop's ביעור applies, you check only the land you are in, all of its regions together.

phrases.english: We learned there [in a mishna]:
phrases.notes: The משנה is in מסכת שביעית, chapter 9.

phrases.english: There are three lands with regard to removal:
Judea, Transjordan, and the Galilee.
And there are three lands within each and every one of them.
phrases.notes: Mountains, valley, and plain.

phrases.english: And why did they say 'three lands for removal'?
phrases.notes: Why speak only of the three big lands, if each one is divided further?

phrases.english: So that people may eat in each and every one
until the last [region] within it runs out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the date ברייתא to a related משנה about the regions of ביעור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביעור is measured per each of the three lands. Within a land, eating continues until the crop is gone from its last region.

steps.title: Where is this rule learned from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that ביעור follows the land as a whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה for the rule in the משנה. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a rule but no reason. The גמרא wants to know why availability of a crop anywhere in the land permits eating, and why each land is judged separately.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these words?' A standard request for the source of a law.

phrases.english: From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural basis of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches ביעור depends on the crop being available in the field, measured by region.

steps.title: The verse: wild animals in the field decide for animals at home
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר עוקבא, quoting רבי יוסי בר חנינא, learns the rule from 'ולבהמתך ולחיה אשר בארצך'. As long as wild animals can eat a crop in the field, you may feed it to your animals at home. Once it is gone for them, it must be gone from your house too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר עוקבא said in the name of רבי יוסי בר חנינא: The verse says, 'And for your cattle and for the wild animals that are in your land.' As long as wild animals eat this crop from the field, you may feed it to the animal in your house. Once it is gone for the wild animals in the field, remove it from your animal in the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. It ties what you may keep at home to what wild animals can still find in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'your cattle' (at home) next to 'the wild animals in your land' (in the field). This teaches that the two are linked: your right to keep the produce lasts only as long as the produce is still free for wild animals. That is why fruit animals cannot reach (as in step 1) does not count. The word 'בארצך' hints that this is judged within a given land.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse says.' This introduces a פסוק as proof.
Your domestic animal, kept at home.
A wild animal living in the field.
'Finish it off' or remove: the command of ביעור.

steps.confusionAlert: בהמה here means the domestic animal at home, and חיה means the wild animal in the field. The wild animal sets the rule for the domestic one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core idea behind all of ביעור: produce of שביעית is ownerless and shared, so you may keep it only while it is still available to all, even to wild animals.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Ukva said
that Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
The verse says:
"And for your cattle and for the beasts that are in your land" (Leviticus 25:7).

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁחַיָּה אוֹכֶלֶת מִן הַשָּׂדֶה —
phrases.english: As long as the wild animal eats from the field —
feed the domestic animal that is in the house;
once it has run out for the wild animal in the field —
remove it for your domestic animal from the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנא הני מילי question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the domestic animal at home to the wild animal in the field. Produce may be kept as long as wild animals can still find it, and must be removed once it is gone for them.

steps.title: Wild animals stay within their own land
steps.stepSummary: A received tradition: wild animals of יהודה do not live off the produce of the גליל, and those of the גליל do not live off the produce of יהודה. So each land is judged on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we have a tradition that a wild animal in יהודה does not grow up on the fruits of the גליל, and a wild animal in the גליל does not grow up on the fruits of יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a known fact about nature. It finishes the proof by explaining why the three lands are measured separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 taught that ביעור depends on what wild animals can find. This tradition adds that wild animals move around within their own land but do not cross into another land. So produce in one land is not 'available to the wild animals' of another land, and each land has its own ביעור. Within a land, though, animals roam between all its regions, so the regions combine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We have learned by tradition.' A fact handed down, not derived from a פסוק.
Grows up on, lives off.
Fruits or produce.

steps.whatToRemember: ביעור of שביעית produce depends on whether the crop is still available to wild animals in the field (from 'ולבהמתך ולחיה'). Wild animals stay within their own land, so each of the three lands (יהודה, עבר הירדן, גליל) is judged separately. Within each land, all its smaller regions count together.

phrases.english: And we have learned by tradition:
that a wild animal in Judea does not
grow up on the fruits of the Galilee,
and a wild animal in the Galilee does not
grow up on the fruits of Judea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from step 4, explaining why the משנה's lands are measured separately.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because wild animals do not cross between lands, availability to wild animals, and therefore ביעור, is measured separately in each land.

steps.title: A dispute about שביעית fruit taken out of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the fruit is removed wherever it is. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it must go back to ארץ ישראל, because the פסוק says 'בארצך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Fruits that left ארץ ישראל for outside the land must be removed wherever they are. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: they must go back to their place and be removed there, because it says 'in your land'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about what to do with שביעית fruit that was taken out of ארץ ישראל when the time for ביעור comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says ביעור can be done anywhere. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says ביעור belongs only in ארץ ישראל, so the fruit must be brought back. He learns this from the word 'בארצך' in the same פסוק used in Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This opens a ברייתא.
Outside ארץ ישראל
They are removed (they get ביעור)
They must return to their place

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Fruits that left the Land of Israel
phrases.notes: This means שביעית produce.

phrases.english: to outside the Land
are removed in any place where they are.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
They must return to their place and be removed there,
because it is stated: 'in your land'.
phrases.notes: From the same פסוק: 'ולבהמתך ולחיה אשר בארצך'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule about the three lands inside ארץ ישראל to a new question: produce that left ארץ ישראל entirely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: removal can be done anywhere. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the produce must be returned and removed in ארץ ישראל, based on 'בארצך'.

steps.title: Wasn't that verse already used for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'בארצך' was already used in Step 4 to teach that each land is judged on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already took that word out for a different lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's source. The word 'בארצך' was already used for another rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, 'אשר בארצך' taught that ביעור follows each separate land. One word normally cannot be the source for two different rules. So how can רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also use it to require returning produce to ארץ ישראל?

keyTerms.meaning: 'But you already took it out (used it) for something else'

phrases.english: But didn't you already use it (for another lesson)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר used in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's use of 'בארצך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word was already 'used up' for the rule that each land is judged separately (Step 4). It cannot also be the source for a second rule.

steps.title: The verse can be read two ways
steps.stepSummary: Read the word as both 'בארץ' (the Land) and 'בארצך' (your land), or learn the second rule from the extra word 'מאשר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as 'in the land' and also as 'in your land'. Or else: learn it from the extra words 'that are in your land'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the פסוק contains enough to teach both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: קרי ביה means we read the word as if it said two things at once. 'בארץ' (the Land) teaches that removal belongs in ארץ ישראל. 'בארצך' (your land) teaches that each land inside it is judged separately. Second answer: the extra word 'אשר' in 'אשר בארצך' supplies the second rule, since the Torah could have written just 'בארצך'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Read into it.' The word is read in two ways.
Alternatively

steps.whatToRemember: One word, read in two ways (or with its extra words), teaches two rules. 'The Land' means ביעור only in ארץ ישראל. 'Your land' means each of the three lands is judged separately.

phrases.english: Read into it both 'in the land' and 'in your land',
alternatively: from 'that are in your land'.
phrases.notes: The extra word 'אשר' gives a second teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Double reading of the verse / extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word can only teach one rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches two rules: removal belongs in ארץ ישראל, and each land is judged separately.

steps.title: רב ספרא asks what the הלכה is as he leaves ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא is leaving ארץ ישראל with שביעית wine. He asks his escorts whether רבי אבהו ruled like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא left ארץ ישראל for outside the land. He had a jug of שביעית wine with him. רב הונא בריה דרב איקא and רב כהנא escorted him. He asked them: Did anyone hear from רבי אבהו whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that tests the dispute. This step sets up the question, and the answers come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the halacha follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, רב ספרא would have to bring the wine back to ארץ ישראל for ביעור. If not, he can remove it wherever he is. So he wants a ruling from רבי אבהו, a leading authority in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A jug of wine
They escorted him
Is there anyone who heard?

phrases.english: Rav Safra went out from the Land of Israel
to outside the Land.
He had with him a jug of Sabbatical-year wine.

phrases.aramaic: לַוּוֹ בַּהֲדֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Ika escorted him
and Rav Kahana.
He said to them: Is there anyone who heard
from Rabbi Abbahu

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: whether the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא נְפַק מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's dispute to a practical case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי אבהו rule like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (return the produce to ארץ ישראל)?

steps.title: רב כהנא: רבי אבהו ruled like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to him: This is what רבי אבהו said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The first student answers רב ספרא with a strict report in the name of רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this report, רב ספרא would have to bring his wine back to ארץ ישראל for ביעור.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to him:
This is what Rabbi Abbahu said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to רב ספרא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The produce must be returned.

steps.title: רב הונא: רבי אבהו ruled against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב איקא reports the opposite: the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב איקא said to him: This is what רבי אבהו said: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The second student gives the opposite report in the name of the same רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two conflicting reports of one teacher's ruling. According to this one, רב ספרא may remove the wine wherever he is.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha does not follow

steps.confusionAlert: Both students quote the same רבי אבהו. The argument is about what רבי אבהו actually said, not about the logic of the law.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Ika said to him:
This is what Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: The halacha does not follow Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts רב כהנא's report in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Removal may be done anywhere.

steps.title: רב ספרא relies on רב הונא's report
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא decides to rely on רב הונא. He is precise and learns exactly from his teacher's mouth, like רחבה of פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: Hold on to this rule of רב הונא, because he is careful and learns teachings exactly from his teacher's mouth, like רחבה of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא settles the conflict by choosing the report of the student known for precise transmission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is the reliability of the transmitter, not leniency or strictness. רב הונא is compared to רחבה, who was famous for keeping his teacher's exact words. The next step gives an example of רחבה's precision.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold it in your hand (rely on it)
A rule or principle
He is precise
Teachings or rulings

steps.whatToRemember: When two students report conflicting rulings from one teacher, rely on the one known for precise transmission. Here that is רב הונא, so removal may be done outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:

phrases.aramaic: נְקוֹט הָא כְּלָלָא דְּרַב הוּנָא בִּידָךְ,
phrases.english: Hold this principle of Rav Huna in your hand,
for he is precise and learns teachings
from the mouth of his teacher
like Rachava of Pumbedita.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקוֹט הָא כְּלָלָא דְּרַב הוּנָא בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the conflicting reports of Steps 10 and 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Follow רב הונא: the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, because רב הונא is a precise transmitter.

steps.title: An example of רחבה's precise wording
steps.stepSummary: רחבה quoted רב יהודה's exact word 'סטיו' to describe the double colonnade of the הר הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רחבה said in the name of רב יהודה: The הר הבית was a double colonnade, a colonnade inside a colonnade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the comparison by showing how carefully רחבה kept his teacher's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רחבה used his teacher's rare word 'סטיו' instead of the common word 'אצטבא'. This shows he kept even the exact language. רב הונא is praised as being this careful too.

keyTerms.meaning: Colonnade (a row of pillars)
Double
The Temple Mount

phrases.english: As Rachava said that Rav Yehuda said:
The Temple Mount was a double colonnade,
a colonnade within a colonnade.
phrases.notes: He kept his teacher's word 'סטיו'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the precision of רחבה mentioned in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רחבה, and by comparison רב הונא, transmitted their teachers' words exactly
steps.raayaSupportSource: רחבה's quote of רב יהודה using the exact word 'סטיו'

steps.title: רב יוסף criticizes relying on the lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף applies a פסוק from הושע as a criticism: whoever rules leniently is the one he listens to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף read this verse about him: 'My people ask their stick, and its staff tells them.' Whoever is lenient with him, that is who tells him the law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף sharply criticizes רב ספרא's choice, as if he simply picked the lenient opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a wordplay: 'מקלו' (his staff) sounds like 'מיקל' (one who is lenient). רב יוסף suggests that רב ספרא's real reason was convenience, not precision. This challenges the decision of Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: He read (a verse) about him
His staff or stick
The one who is lenient

steps.whyThisMatters: It warns against choosing rulings just because they are lenient and convenient.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef read about him:
'My people ask counsel of their stick,
and its staff tells them' (Hosea 4:12).
Whoever is lenient with him, he is the one who 'tells' him.
phrases.notes: A wordplay on מקלו / מיקל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes רב ספרא's decision in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's reliance on רב הונא's lenient report
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Choosing the lenient report looks like picking whatever is convenient, not following the more reliable tradition.

steps.title: רבי אילעאי cuts down a tree with young dates
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי אילעאי cut down a palm tree that held unripe dates during שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעאי cut down a palm tree with unripe dates of שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about something רבי אילעאי did. This story sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young dates growing on the tree were שביעית produce. By cutting the tree down, רבי אילעאי caused those young dates to be lost. The next step will ask how this was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut down / chopped
Unripe, young dates
The seventh year (Sabbatical Year), when produce has special holiness

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai chopped down
phrases.notes: He cut down a palm tree.

phrases.english: unripe dates of the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: The tree still had young dates on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the laws of שביעית, separate from the earlier discussion about relying on רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אילעאי cut down a palm tree bearing unripe שביעית dates.

steps.title: How could he destroy שביעית produce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אילעאי could do this, since the תורה says שביעית produce is for eating and not for destroying.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? The תורה says 'for eating', and not for destroying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילעאי's action. Cutting the tree seems to break the rule against wasting שביעית produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says שביעית produce is 'לאכלה' – for you to eat. The חכמים learn from this that you may eat it, but you may not destroy it. Cutting a tree with dates on it destroys those dates.

keyTerms.meaning: How did he do this? (a challenge to someone's action)
'For eating' – from the פסוק about שביעית produce
Destruction, loss, waste
'The Merciful One' – a name for God, used for the Torah

phrases.english: How did he do this?!
phrases.notes: A sharp challenge.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said: 'for eating',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:ו

phrases.english: and not for destruction.
phrases.notes: The rule learned from the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action told in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעאי's cutting of the palm tree with young dates.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שביעית produce may only be eaten, not destroyed (לאכלה ולא להפסד), and cutting the tree destroys the dates.

steps.title: Suggested defense: unripe dates are not yet fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ban on destroying applies only once the produce counts as fruit, and these young dates did not yet count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: this applies only where it has reached the stage of fruit, but where it has not reached the stage of fruit, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense of רבי אילעאי. This defense is only being set up so it can be knocked down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the rule 'not for destroying' only protects real fruit. If young dates are not yet 'fruit', cutting them down would not be wasting שביעית produce.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say' – introduces a possible answer that will be rejected
This applies only...
Has 'gone down' into fruit – reached the stage of being called fruit

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's real answer. 'וכי תימא' introduces an answer the גמרא is about to reject.

phrases.english: And if you will say: this applies
phrases.notes: Introducing a suggested defense.

phrases.english: where it has reached the stage of fruit,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא נָחֵית לְפֵירָא — לָא.
phrases.english: but where it has not reached the stage of fruit — no.
phrases.notes: Then there would be no ban.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a defense against the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to produce that has reached the fruit stage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The young dates were not yet 'fruit', so cutting them is not destroying שביעית produce.

steps.title: רב נחמן shows that very young dates already count as fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's ruling about ערלה date-coverings proves that even very young dates are called fruit, so the suggested defense fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן say in the name of רבה בר אבוה: those date-coverings of ערלה are forbidden, since they became a protector for the fruit. And when are they a protector for the fruit? When the dates are tiny, and yet he calls them fruit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense from step 17. It brings a ruling that treats tiny young dates as real fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן forbids the covering around ערלה dates because it protects the fruit. That covering only protects the dates when they are tiny (כופרי). Since he calls those tiny dates 'fruit', young dates do count as fruit, and רבי אילעאי's cutting is again a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The sheath / covering around young dates
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, forbidden to eat or benefit from
A protector of the fruit (a peel or shell), treated like the fruit
Very young, tiny dates at the earliest stage

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say
phrases.notes: Introducing the rejection.

phrases.english: that Rabba bar Avuh said:
those orla date-coverings are forbidden,
since they became a protector for the fruit.
phrases.notes: A protector is treated like the fruit itself.

phrases.english: And when is it a protector for the fruit?
phrases.notes: The גמרא now draws the point.

phrases.english: When they are tiny young dates, and yet he calls them fruit!
phrases.notes: So young dates already count as fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the defense proposed in step 17, bringing back the challenge of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that young dates are not yet fruit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן's ruling on ערלה coverings assumes that tiny dates (כופרי) are already fruit.

steps.title: רב נחמן follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's view follows רבי יוסי, a minority opinion; רבי אילעאי can follow the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said his ruling according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רב נחמן's ruling is based on one specific opinion. The next step will show the source of that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only רבי יוסי holds that very young produce is fruit, then רב נחמן's ruling is not everyone's view. רבי אילעאי could follow the רבנן, who say young produce is not yet fruit, so cutting the tree was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of רבי יוסי

phrases.english: Rav Nachman, who said it, holds like Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: His ruling follows one opinion only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 18 by limiting רב נחמן's ruling to one opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the opposing ruling to a minority opinion (רבי יוסי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's ruling shows that everyone treats young dates as fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי יוסי holds this; רבי אילעאי can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה: רבי יוסי says a סמדר is fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבי יוסי forbids the סמדר because it is fruit, and the רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יוסי says: the סמדר is forbidden, because it is fruit. And the רבנן disagree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the answer in step 19. It shows that רבי יוסי counts very early fruit as fruit, and that the רבנן disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סמדר is a grape cluster at its earliest stage, just after the flowers fall. רבי יוסי forbids it as ערלה because it is already fruit. Since the רבנן argue, the majority view is that such early produce is not yet fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A grape cluster at its earliest stage, right after the blossoms fall
And the רבנן disagree with him

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yosei says:
phrases.notes: The source of רבי יוסי's view.

phrases.english: the grape bud is forbidden, because it is fruit,
phrases.notes: Forbidden as ערלה.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis disagree with him.
phrases.notes: The majority says it is not yet fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the answer in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי treats earliest-stage produce as fruit, and that the רבנן disagree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about סמדר and ערלה.

steps.title: רב שימי: do the רבנן disagree about other trees?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי מנהרדעא objects: maybe the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי only about grapes, but not about other trees like dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי of נהרדעא challenged it: do the רבנן really disagree with רבי יוסי about other trees?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי attacks the answer from step 19. He questions whether the argument between רבי יוסי and the רבנן covers all trees, or only grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 20 spoke about grapes (סמדר). If the רבנן agree with רבי יוסי about other trees, then young dates would count as fruit for everyone. That would bring back the problem with רבי אילעאי's act.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly challenged it
Do they really disagree? (a rhetorical challenge)
Other trees (besides grapevines)

phrases.english: Rav Shimi of Neharde'a strongly objected:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: And do the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yosei
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: they do not.

phrases.english: regarding other trees?
phrases.notes: Maybe they argue only about grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of steps 19–20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי in a way that would cover dates.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן's argument may only be about grapes; for other trees, even they may agree that early produce is fruit.

steps.title: The משנה about cutting trees in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי begins quoting a משנה about when one may no longer cut down trees in שביעית, to prove his point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: From when may one no longer cut down trees in שביעית? בית שמאי say: all trees, from when they produce fruit. And בית הלל say: carob trees, from when they form chains, and the vines...
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי brings a משנה to support his challenge. The quote continues on the next amud, where בית הלל's full list will show the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a tree in שביעית is forbidden once its fruit counts as fruit, because that would destroy שביעית produce. בית שמאי set the point for all trees at the earliest stage, when fruit first appears. בית הלל give different stages for different trees, and their list will show how they treat other trees.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (introduces a source used as a challenge)
Cut down (trees)
From when they bring out fruit (the earliest stage)
Carob trees
From when they form chains (of carob pods)
Grapevines

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: Introducing the proof.

phrases.aramaic: מֵאֵימָתַי אֵין קוֹצְצִין אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית?
phrases.english: From when may one no longer cut down trees in the Sabbatical Year?
phrases.notes: Because cutting would destroy the fruit.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
all trees, from when they bring out fruit,
phrases.notes: The earliest stage.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say:
phrases.notes: They divide by type of tree.

phrases.english: carob trees, from when they form chains,
and the vines,
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּנַן: מֵאֵימָתַי אֵין קוֹצְצִין אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind רב שימי's challenge in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן may agree with רבי יוסי about trees other than grapevines.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית about when one may no longer cut down trees.
